public_rationale: Read plainly, the claim says that by August 2025 low-quality AI content had spread widely across many domains and was causing real harm. Evidence from before the post backs this. Ahrefs found AI-generated content in 74.2% of 900,000 new web pages in April 2025. Deezer reported in April 2025 that over 18% of daily music uploads were fully AI-generated. By May 2025, a database of court decisions recorded 116 cases in 12 countries where AI-hallucinated content had been submitted in legal filings. That shows large volumes in at least three separate domains and documented harm in law. 'Serious' is a value judgment and 'ubiquitous' is hyperbole. The verdict rests on reading them as 'harmful' and 'widespread', which is how an ordinary reader would take them.
limitations: Key terms are evaluative or hyperbolic, so the result depends on the plain reading.
Some measures count AI-assisted content, which is not necessarily slop.
The detection figures come from companies with their own tools, not audited studies.
Not every domain the post names (politics, journalism, education) is covered by a cited measurement.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: The problem of AI slop/enshittification is serious and ubiquitous.

statement.excerpt: He still prefers “enshittification” to “slop”, but the problem is both serious and ubiquitous no matter what you call it.

from_speaker: the problem is both serious and ubiquitous
no matter what you call it
our_interpretation: Plain reading: by the post date (August 2025), low-quality or erroneous AI-generated content was widespread across many domains, not just one niche, and it was causing documented harm.
'Ubiquitous' is read as 'widespread across many domains', not literally present everywhere.
'Serious' is an evaluative word. It is read as 'causing documented real-world harm', such as sanctions on lawyers for fake AI citations or platforms flooded with AI content.
No period is named. The claim describes an ongoing state, so the target period is January 2025 through the post date (2025-08-04).
criteria.support_condition: Credible measurements or records from before the post showing large volumes of AI-generated content in several separate domains (for example the web, music, legal filings), plus documented harms.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Credible measurements showing AI-generated content was rare or confined to a few domains in mid-2025, or that documented harms were negligible.

evidence.excerpt: We analyzed 900,000 newly created web pages in April 2025 and found that 74.2% of them contained AI-generated content.
evidence.explanation: Shows AI-generated content was present in most new web pages in April 2025. This supports 'widespread'. Caveats: the measurement uses Ahrefs' own detector, and most pages were mixed human-and-AI rather than pure AI.

evidence.excerpt: 20,000 completely AI-generated tracks are added to its music service on a daily basis, making up "over 18% of all uploaded content" the platform receives every day.
evidence.explanation: Shows that fully AI-generated tracks were a large and growing share of music uploads in a second domain. The same article says Spotify faces the same issue.

evidence.excerpt: Damien's database has 116 cases from 12 different countries
evidence.explanation: Records court decisions in 12 countries confirming that AI-hallucinated content was submitted in legal filings. This is documented harm in law, a third domain. The post also notes that 20 of the cases came in May 2025 alone.
